correctness.rationale: The half-open unit cells give exact images: each central cell covers the k opposite cells, and each outer cell moves inwards one cell. Every closed graph word visits both hubs, so the composition of the inverse branches on closures has exactly one fixed point by contraction. If it lies in the actual cells, the word and point determine one another. Endpoints must be followed with a fixed one-sided sign because all branches are increasing. The periodic right germs trace 0→−k→…→−1→0, using the actual map; the periodic left germs trace 0→k→…→1→0, using the excluded upper boundaries. All other endpoint germs are preperiodic by inward translation. Exactly the k+1 marked starting positions of the left-germ cycle are surplus when k+1 divides n. Eliminating the outer chains gives one excursion of each length 1 through k, hence determinant 1−S_k(t)^2 and the one-cycle numerator. The graph is strongly connected and has return lengths two and three, so Perron–Frobenius and the bounded correction give eventual positivity and the exponential growth rate. The same graph gives the symbolic entropy. The positive Perron root grows with k and tends to 2 by beta_k=2−beta_k^(−k). Central affine fixed roots lie outside their cells and no translation fixes a point. A separate exact rational enumeration for k=2,…,5 through n=8 agreed; e.g. k=2 yields 0,2,3,6,10,17,28,46. Finite checks do not establish the all-period identity or asymptotic.

value.rationale: At a parameter boundary already used in this map family, exact integer gain replaces finite hardware or orbit experiments by an all-period invariant. The model-specific endpoint correction is essential for physical cycle counts and quantifies exactly where a graph-only census is wrong. The result also makes the full dependence of periodic growth on integer gain explicit, without claiming a canonical entropy for other discontinuous-map conventions.
